statement: Call an index i good for (nums,k) when 0 <= i < n, (if 0 <= i-k < n then nums[i] > nums[i-k]), and (if 0 <= i+k < n then nums[i] > nums[i+k]). Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the sum of nums[i] over all i with 0 <= i < n that are good for (nums,k). The sum over an empty set of indices is 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2) with k interpreted as an integer; and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r for every input satisfying the preconditions; equivalently, it never fails on such inputs.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= (sum_{i=0}^{n-1} nums[i]) - 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: If there is an integer c with 1 <= c <= 1000 such that nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < n, then whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Assume n = 2 (hence k = 1). Whenever the function returns a result r: if nums[0] > nums[1] then r = nums[0]; if nums[0] < nums[1] then r = nums[1]; if nums[0] = nums[1] then r = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: If nums[i] > nums[i+1] for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, then whenever the function returns a result r, r = sum_{i=0}^{k-1} nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: If nums[i] < nums[i+1] for every i with 0 <= i < n-1, then whenever the function returns a result r, r = sum_{i=n-k}^{n-1} nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let rev be the array of length n with rev[i] = nums[n-1-i] for 0 <= i < n. Whenever the function returns r for (nums,k) and r' for (rev,k), r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Call an index i good for (nums,k) when 0 <= i < n, (if 0 <= i-k < n then nums[i] > nums[i-k]), and (if 0 <= i+k < n then nums[i] > nums[i+k]). For every integer i with 0 <= i < n, if i is good for (nums,k), then whenever the function returns a result r, r >= nums[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Call an index i good for (nums,k) when 0 <= i < n, (if 0 <= i-k < n then nums[i] > nums[i-k]), and (if 0 <= i+k < n then nums[i] > nums[i+k]). Let nums' be the array with nums'[i] = nums[i]+c, and let g be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n that are good for (nums,k). Whenever the function returns r for (nums,k) and r' for (nums',k), r' = r + c*g.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let c be an integer such that 1 <= nums[i]+c <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let nums' be the array with nums'[i] = c*nums[i] for 0 <= i < n. Whenever the function returns r for (nums,k) and r' for (nums',k), r' = c*r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). Assume 2 <= n <= 100; 1 <= k <= floor(n/2); and 1 <= nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n. Let c be an integer with c >= 1 such that 1 <= c*nums[i] <= 1000 for every i with 0 <= i < n.
